content_flow.text: BSc Interior Design full form is Bachelor of Science in Interior Design, a 3-year-long UG degree course focused on enhancing the skills and technical knowledge of the students in designing interior spaces. Here you get to learn to design comfortable spaces and plan the interiors of commercial or residential buildings, apartments, ensuring functionality, safety, and even aesthetic ambience.

Design Principles, Space Planning, Lighting Design, Furniture Design, History of Interior Design, and Drawing and Visualization are the core of the study of this course. Anyone with a Class 12 certificate from a recognized board with at least 60% aggregate score can get admission to this course.

You’ll find more than 200 colleges in India offering the BSc in Interior Design course. The average course fee ranges between INR 27,000 and INR 10 Lakh . You can seek career opportunities in fields like Interior Design companies, Entertainment, Fashion Studios, Hospitality, Event Management , etc.
If interested, you can continue reading the article for more details on the Bachelor of Interior Design course in India.

content.text: The four-year Bachelor of Science in Interior Design degree emphasises the approaches and ideas for comprehending human behaviour and creating livable places that meet client needs. To design the interior spaces, candidates for this course comprehend the inner and exterior layout of any facility.

content.text: Subjects like Lighting Design, Sustainable Design, Space Planning and Layout, Materials and Finishes, etc. are covered in this course. Candidates who are interested in an interior design job can take this course. Candidates who have a strong sense of vision and are creative must definitely enrol in this programme. They must be skilled at creating plans and have the ability to oversee both the client's budget and the enterprise itself.

Candidates should enrol in this programme and use interior design as a means of showcasing their original innovations and ability to adapt to changing circumstances. faqs.question: What is the BSc Interior Design course duration in India?

content.text: The general BSc Interior Design course duration in India is 3 years , which is spread across 6 semesters. You can get admission to the course after completing Class 12 in any stream with at least 50% marks in board exams and clearing relevant entrance tests for top Design institutes. Several colleges also give admission based on Class 12 board exam marks and other rounds like GD, PI, and portfolio submission.

faqs.question: Is Science stream mandatory in Class 12 for BSc Interior Design eligibility?

content.text: No , passing Class 12 from the Science stream is not mandatory to be eligible for BSc Interior Designing program. BSc in Interior Design programme covers technical and scientific elements related to Interior Design such as lighting, sustainable practices, etc. However, you can pursue BSc Interior Design regardless of the stream you had in Class 12.

faqs.question: Is there any age limit for BSc Interior Design course?

content.text: No, in most cases you don't have to worry about the age limit while taking admission in BSc in Interior Design course. However, some colleges may have minimum age limit of 16 years. As far as I know there is no cap on the maximum age limit.

faqs.question: Can I pursue BSc Interior Design after completing Diploma?

content.text: Yes, you can pursue BSc in Interior Design after a Diploma if the Diploma is considered equivalent to Class 12. You can enroll yourself in the course either after completing Class 12 or Class 10 followed by a 3-year Diploma.

Syllabus for Entrance Exam
Here are some important BSc Interior Design exams' syllabus.

rows.Exam Syllabus: The UCEED entrance covers 2 parts: Part A and Part B. Part A is an Online, Computer-based Test (CBT) including NAT, MSQ, and MCQ. However, Part B is conducted offline and includes Sketching.
Topics include Design Outline for Beginners, Colour Terminology, Inspiration & Design Development, Design Theory, Elements & Principles Of Design, etc.

The NIFT entrance exam is conducted in 2 parts: the Creative Ability Test (CAT) and the General Ability Test (GAT). The CAT includes topics such as Creative Ability, Power of Observation, etc. Whereas the GAT includes Aptitude, Communication Ability, etc.
The CUET syllabus is divided into 3 sections: Language, Domain Specific, and General Test.

questions.question_text: Is TDV good for Interior Design? Looking for honest feedback on faculty, studio culture, projects and overall learning experience.

answers.answer_text: I'm studying Interior Design here, and what stands out is that you're in the studio almost all the time. You don't just submit work and forget it — you keep reworking the same design after feedback, which really improves your thinking. Faculty push you a lot, sometimes it feels annoying, but later you realise why. The studio culture is intense near submissions, but very chill otherwise. You learn less from lectures and more from mistakes, discussions, and long studio hours. It's not fancy or easy, but if you stay involved, you genuinely improve.
